video.title: The Easiest Way to Actually Make Money With AI

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Corey, who sells a $1,000 'AI assessment' (audit) to small businesses. A voice agent (Annie, built on a voice-AI platform) interviews the owner for 10-20 minutes, another AI agent turns the transcript into a report (Docx to Gamma) recommending off-the-shelf tools, and a follow-up call upsells process optimisation, Zapier/Make automations, custom GPT knowledge systems, CRM setups and speed-to-lead agents at $1.5k-$5k+. Corey then lists tactics for finding customers with no following: local AI meetups, door knocking, free audits for a peer group, and office hours. Key takeaway: you only need to be one step ahead of the client, and a higher-priced audit makes the upsell easier.

speakers.name: Corey
speakers.description: Runs AI assessment business 'Return My Time' with partner Nick; hosts the Build with AI podcast

ideas.name: AI assessment (audit) for small businesses
ideas.one_liner: Voice-agent interview of a business owner, AI-generated report of off-the-shelf tool recommendations, sold at $1,000 with follow-up call and upsells.
ideas.business_model: One-off paid assessment that feeds upsell project work
ideas.customer: Small businesses with teams, ideally 5-50 employees (realtors, business brokers, wedding venues, barber school, mortgage broker)
ideas.problem: Owners don't know where AI and software tools could save them time; most have not adopted even simple tools.
ideas.offer: A 20-30 minute voice-agent conversation, then a report within 48 hours (executive summary, effort vs impact matrix, recommended tools, 4-day quick-win plan, upsell opportunities, financial impact) plus a 30-minute follow-up call.

pricing.model: Fixed fee per assessment, raised over time
pricing.notes: Higher price increases client seriousness and makes a $3.5k upsell feel closer. Called 'assessment' rather than 'audit' as it sounds less aggressive.

acquisition_channels.details: Host a free local AI-for-small-business meetup (Luma, meetup.com); the organiser is seen as the authority.

quote.text: host a local AI meetup in your town, right? You go on Luma, you go on meetup.com and you literally just say, "Hey, AI for small business meetup."
quote.speaker: Corey

acquisition_channels.details: Door-knock local businesses for a conversation about how they use AI, leading with value.
Offered free audits to a local CEO peer group of 11-12 people; got testimonials and warm upsell contacts.
Free AI meetup / weekly or monthly office hours inside a realtor's office; brokers in charge may want workshops. Captured emails at the door.

ideas.delivery: A voice agent calls the owner and asks questions from a master question bank by industry. Transcript goes to a second AI agent (multiple skills) that cleans it, searches AI tools, and outputs a docx. The docx is uploaded to a Gamma template. Corey sends it within 48 hours and presents it on a follow-up call. A beginner version is a Zoom call plus Claude.
unit_economics_claims: Sold at $1,000 with almost no cost, nearly pure margin
Example report: 8 hours a week saved, about $3,200 a month value vs $59 a month tool cost
ideas.startup_cost: Near zero (Claude subscription, Gamma, voice agent platform); exact costs not stated
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated; the first 2-3 assessments were free, then $200

acquisition.how: Meetups, door knocking and peer-group outreach are in person; only the follow-up and event promotion can be automated.

onboarding.how: Owner calls a number any time; the voice agent runs the interview.

delivery.how: Agents build the report with Gamma; the human checks the tools and walks through the report on a call.

billing.how: Fixed-fee invoice or Stripe link; not described in the transcript.

support.how: A human follow-up call is needed to explain and upsell.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK. Recording calls needs consent and UK GDPR handling of transcripts. Door knocking and meetups are legal. Prices would be in GBP.

risks: Recorded interviews contain business data, so UK GDPR and consent apply
Only works with owners who value their time; solo operators are a worse fit
Quick-win tools are off-the-shelf, so competition and commoditisation are likely

ideas.name: Process optimisation engagement
ideas.one_liner: Fix a broken, over-long business process before automating it.
ideas.problem: A task taking 10 hours a week may be a 15-step process that should be 7 steps.
ideas.offer: Redesign of one process, sold separately from the automation build.

pricing.notes: Fixing the process and automating it are separate engagements.

acquisition_channels.details: Upsell to assessment clients on the follow-up call.

ideas.delivery: Consultant maps and redesigns the process with the client.
unit_economics_claims: Sold for $3-4k at a time, described as a $3-5k upsell all day

acquisition.how: Upsell from the assessment report and call.

delivery.how: Needs human judgement and client workshops.

risks: Hard to scope; value is hard to quantify

quotes.text: we've successfully sold process optimization engagements for $3 to $4,000 at a time just to fix one process
quotes.speaker: Corey

ideas.name: Zapier / Make.com automation builds
ideas.one_liner: Build simple two-step automations for assessment clients.
ideas.problem: Staff spend time on manual tasks such as setting up project templates.
ideas.offer: Zapier or Make automation; example formats Asana projects automatically for each new client.

acquisition_channels.details: Upsell after assessment or free audit.

ideas.delivery: Consultant builds the zap; 30 minutes of operations manager time per client was removed.
unit_economics_claims: $1,500 Zapier build saved 30 minutes per new client

delivery.how: Agents can build simple zaps with review.

quotes.text: we did a build for them $1,500 a Zapier automation to essentially format their ASA projects in a certain way every time they got a new client
quotes.speaker: Corey

ideas.name: Custom GPT knowledge system
ideas.one_liner: Train a custom GPT on a listing's marketing package to answer repetitive buyer questions.
ideas.customer: Business brokers and similar professionals who get repetitive enquiries
ideas.problem: A business broker gets 200-400 emails in the first week of a listing, 95% repeating the same 10 questions.
ideas.offer: Custom GPT trained on the listing's SIM with a system prompt that restricts what is revealed.

pricing.notes: Price not stated; the system prompt can be resold for every future listing.

ideas.delivery: Build a custom GPT with guarded system prompt; reuse for each listing.
unit_economics_claims: Handles 95% of Q&A so only 5% reach the inbox

delivery.how: Mostly agent-built with human review of guardrails.

uk_applicability.notes: Works; check confidentiality and data handling for buyer data.

risks: Leaking confidential financials if the prompt is weak

quotes.text: we create a custom GPT trained on your SIM, and we just give that to buyers so that that can handle 95% of the Q&A workload
quotes.speaker: Corey

ideas.name: Speed-to-lead AI agent
ideas.one_liner: AI agent that replies instantly to web-form leads and books appointments or tours.
ideas.customer: Service businesses that miss leads (e.g. wedding venue)
ideas.problem: Leads go elsewhere if not answered within about 10 minutes; staff are busy on tours.
ideas.offer: Make.com agent that personalises replies, converses and schedules a call or tour, trained on FAQs.

acquisition_channels.details: Corey's first paid AI engagement, for the wedding venue.

ideas.delivery: Built in Make.com (or Zapier) with an LLM trained on the client's FAQs.
unit_economics_claims: Average deal $11k with 40% close rate from tours; one or two extra tours a month adds about $11k

delivery.how: Agent runs unattended after the build.

uk_applicability.notes: Works; the PECR limits apply to outbound messages, but replying to inbound form submissions is fine.

quotes.text: their average deal size is 11 grand and they know that if they get somebody on a tour they have a 40% close rate
quotes.speaker: Corey

tactics.name: Pilot free, then step the price up
steps: Do the first 2-3 assessments free for testimonials and to fix process kinks
Charge $200, then $500, then $1,000
Use the $1,000 anchor so a $3.5k upsell feels like a small jump

quote.text: you're almost shooting yourself in the foot later on by being cheap early on
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Assessment to upsell funnel
steps: Run the voice or Zoom interview
Send the report within 48 hours with a booking link for a 30-minute follow-up
Screen-share and walk through quick wins
Introduce upsell opportunities and the financial-impact slide
Put the financial impact slide at the top as a hook (host suggestion)

tactics.name: Prompt Claude to build the report
steps: Attach the interview transcript to Claude
Ask it to find off-the-shelf AI or software tools that fix the identified pain points
Tell it to search directories like Futurepedia
Ask Claude how each tool is implemented before the follow-up call

tactics.name: Free local AI meetup or office hours
steps: Ask a well-connected realtor to host a free AI event at their office
Give a 20-25 minute pure-value talk, no pitch
Capture emails at the door
Offer weekly or monthly AI office hours at realtor offices or co-working spaces
Follow up with assessments

tactics.name: Specialise in one upsell
steps: Pick one upsell, such as a custom GPT, as the bread and butter
Productise it
Prefer an upsell tied to revenue or savings, such as a speed-to-lead agent

tools_mentioned.name: Claude
tools_mentioned.purpose: Analyse transcripts, research tools, build skills and diagrams

tools_mentioned.name: Gamma
tools_mentioned.purpose: Turn the docx into a branded report

warnings.warning: Asking clients to screen-record work with Loom was too much friction, so the pilot failed.

quote.text: we found that was just asking too much of people. They hadn't used Loom before. It's too foreign.
quote.speaker: Corey

warnings.warning: Don't be a jack of all trades on upsells; specialise to avoid spreading thin.

quote.text: when you're a jack of all trades, you get spread really thin
quote.speaker: Corey

warnings.warning: Cheap early pricing makes later bigger upsells harder, and low-priced assessments are taken less seriously.
Custom GPT system prompts must block sensitive data such as phone numbers and financials.

lessons.lesson: You only need to be one step ahead of your client, not an expert; about 7 days of study can be enough to sell.

quote.text: You just need to be one step ahead of your average client, which is literally you studying this stuff for like 7 days
quote.speaker: Corey

lessons.lesson: Productise a low-effort diagnostic as an entry offer, then monetise the follow-on projects.
Price signals value: higher entry prices make clients take recommendations seriously and ease upsells.
Remove friction from customer input: a phone number to call beats asking people to record screens.
Pilot free with a warm network to get testimonials and refine the process.
Sell upsells tied directly to revenue or savings, such as speed-to-lead with an $11k deal size.
Start with manual or simple tooling (Zoom plus Claude), then automate the bottleneck step with a voice agent.
Fix the process before automating it.
Being the organiser of a local event makes you the authority.

evidence_quality.rationale: Corey is a first-hand operator with a concrete process, demo and price ladder, but revenue totals, customer counts and conversion rates are not given, and the interview doubles as promotion.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Corey gives away an audit template at audittemplate.ai and promotes his Build with AI podcast; the Go High Level sponsor read and Koerner's TKO Owners community are also promoted.
